Create a place in your apps that shows a paywall, which the app asks for by its slug. --show shows a
paywall there right away; a paywall without a live build creates nothing.

Usage:
  voidhash location create [flags]

Flags:
      --description <description>  Where in the app it is
  -h, --help                       Show help for this command
      --json                       Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --name <name>                What people see, such as Onboarding end
      --project <project>          Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name
                                   (default: this directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet                      Print only ids, one per line
      --show <paywall>             A paywall with a live build to show there right away
      --slug <slug>                What your app asks for (default: made from the name); it cannot
                                   change later

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash location create --name "Onboarding end"
  voidhash location create --name Settings --slug settings --show pro
